source: RC1 deep review DR1-G-2 (round-1-g-host.md); the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-23; RFC 0009 (sentences proposed in the PR)
statement: A session record (a token family) is kept from each write for the shorter of what is left of its lifetime and the refresh token validity (cosec.jwt.token-validity.refresh), so a session nobody refreshes leaves the store with its last refresh token; and a store keeps, for each principal in each tenant, the TokenFamilyStore.SESSIONS_PER_PRINCIPAL (64) sessions that began most recently: creating one more deletes the record of the one that began earliest, live, revoked or ended, whose next refresh is then refused as an unknown session. CoSec's stores count a session before they write its record, so none escapes the count.
guards: spi:InMemorySessionBoundTest#a record nobody refreshes ends with its refresh token, and each write keeps it that long again
spi:InMemorySessionBoundTest#a write never keeps a record past the end of its session
spi:InMemorySessionBoundTest#a principal keeps the sessions that began last, the earliest deleted, revoked or not
spi:InMemorySessionBoundTest#the bound is per principal and per tenant
cocache:SessionBoundTest#a record is kept no longer than its refresh token, from each write
cocache:SessionBoundTest#a principal keeps the sessions that began last, and the earliest is deleted
cocache:SessionBoundTest#the bound is per principal and per tenant
cocache:SessionBoundTest#the index lives as long as the longest session it counts
